Hi all \u0013

Attached a first-pass SDK README and an auth flow diagram. Highlights below, plus attachments: redwood_sdk_setup.md (README), auth_flow.png (diagram).

SDK setup (short):
- Quickstart (node/python): install via pip/npm, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use OAuth token exchange. Sample snippet: 

  // Node example (pseudo)
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({auth: {type: 'oauth', token: process.env.OAUTH_TOKEN}});

Auth options:
- OAuth2 (recommended) with token exchange from Okta; we support short-lived access tokens and rotation via our token service.
- SAML SSO for console access and provisioning; API access still via OAuth2 tokens or service principals.

Routing and model variants:
- Route by latency requirement: route=low_latency -> pinned low-latency quantized model; route=batch -> high-capacity model.
- Automatic fallback: if pinned pool is saturated, requests are redirected to compatible variant with a degraded SLA (configurable).

Embeddings + reranker patterns:
- Bulk upsert strategy: batch upserts (recommended batch size 500-2k vectors) during off-peak windows.
- Real-time upsert for critical items (inventory changes) with a lower-cost quantization profile.
- Reranker flow: retrieve top-K via embedding similarity -> pass candidates to a lightweight reranker model with structured tool-calling output for scoring.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_setup.md (text), auth_flow.png (image)

I'll push these to the shared Drive link as well and can join Thu 10 AM PST.

Hi Samir / team \u0013

Attached is a short prompt_versioning_policy.pdf and a one-page governance checklist. Key items: 

1) Prompt versioning: store system and user-facing prompt templates in Git with semver tags and an approval PR workflow (dev -> security -> legal). Each deployment environment (dev/stage/prod) pins to a specific version hash.

2) Prompt injection mitigations:
- Sanitize untrusted user inputs (explicit allowlists for function/tool params).
- Escape/encode user content when included in system prompts or code blocks.
- Use structured output validation: require JSON schema enforcement and server-side schema validation before taking actions.

3) Red teaming: quarterly red-team cycles + targeted prompt-injection fuzzing for new templates. Maintain test prompts and a regression suite; failures create blocking tickets.

4) Monitoring & rollback: link prompt evals to Canary runs; automatic rollback trigger on degradation of NLU intent metrics or safety checks.

Happy to walk through this during the architecture call. I'll also attach the one-pager to the Drive folder.

Best,
Marissa
